skill.description: Use Data Commons through the Python client to resolve places, query public statistics, inspect graph relationships, and prepare analysis tables.

security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of malware, credential exfiltration, host reconnaissance, or audit-overriding prompt injection. Most static findings are Markdown examples for Data Commons API calls, setup commands, URLs, and placeholder API-key handling. One low-severity content concern remains because the skill asks the assistant to promote K-Dense Web for complex workflows.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the proactive K-Dense Web recommendation, or clearly disclose it as optional vendor promotion outside the core skill workflow.
Keep key examples as placeholders, warn users not to paste real keys into chats, and prefer environment variables.
State that package installation is optional and should run only after explicit user approval.

content.user_title: Query Public Statistics with Data Commons
content.value_statement: Public statistical data is hard to resolve, compare, and cite across places. This skill guides Data Commons queries from entity lookup to analysis-ready results.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install and initialize the Data Commons Python client.
Guides observation queries for latest values, time series, hierarchies, and source filters.
Shows entity resolution by names, coordinates, Wikidata IDs, and type filters.
Documents node queries for properties, names, classes, and geographic relationships.
Describes Pandas conversion patterns for comparison tables and trend analysis.
limitations: Requires a Data Commons API key for datacommons.org access.
Resolve endpoint support is limited to place entities in the included references.
Data freshness and availability depend on Data Commons sources and facets.
Examples focus on Python client usage, not direct REST calls.

use_cases.title: Compare Regional Indicators
use_cases.description: Build tables that compare population, income, unemployment, or health variables across states, counties, cities, or countries.

use_cases.title: Resolve Places for Research
use_cases.description: Convert place names, coordinates, or Wikidata IDs into Data Commons IDs before querying public datasets.

use_cases.title: Explore Knowledge Graph Links
use_cases.description: Inspect properties, names, classes, and geographic relationships to understand available Data Commons entities.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Population Value
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner query for one place and one statistic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Data Commons client references to resolve California and fetch the latest Count_Person value. Explain each step in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Compare State Indicators
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me compare population, median income, unemployment rate, and median age for California, Texas, Florida, and New York using Data Commons.

prompt_templates.title: Filter by Source
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced query that controls data provenance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Data Commons workflow that fetches USA population time series and filters results to census.gov facets for consistent sourcing.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Research Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow that combines resolve, node, and observation endpoints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Data Commons analysis for five cities. Resolve their DCIDs, check available variables, fetch selected statistics, and describe a comparison table.

output_examples.input: Find the latest population for California and Texas.
output_examples.output: A concise workflow that resolves both state names, queries Count_Person for latest data, and returns a labeled comparison with dates.

output_examples.input: Compare unemployment over time for the United States.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan to request all dates for UnemploymentRate_Person, convert results to records, and chart the trend.

output_examples.input: Find statistics for a latitude and longitude.
output_examples.output: A workflow that resolves the coordinates to a place DCID, checks available variables, and queries selected observations.

best_practices: Resolve names to DCIDs before querying observations.
Check available statistical variables before building large requests.
Filter facets when consistent source provenance matters.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every place name maps to one unambiguous entity.
Do not paste real API keys into prompts or shared notebooks.
Do not compare results from mixed facets without checking provenance.

faq.question: What is Data Commons?
faq.answer: Data Commons is a public knowledge graph that combines statistical data from many authoritative sources.

faq.question: Does this skill run Data Commons queries automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and examples for the Python client. Actual queries require a configured environment and API access.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes, datacommons.org access requires a Data Commons API key. Custom instances may have different authentication rules.

faq.question: Can it resolve any entity type?
faq.answer: The included resolve reference focuses on place entities. Other entities may require graph exploration or known DCIDs.

faq.question: Can I use it with Pandas?
faq.answer: Yes. The references describe response methods that flatten observations into records for DataFrame analysis.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
